text:
Anya K: quick heads-up — noticed a drop in prefix cache yield after the keyselector change last night (prefix_hash_v2) :thinking_face:
Samir: saw it too, but need numbers. how big is the delta?
perf-bot: realtime-profile: model=redwood-rlhf-v2-12b route=/chat tenant=acme hit_rate_prev=0.217 hit_rate_now=0.182 token_saved_rate_prev=1420 token_saved_rate_now=1250
Lee: ~3.5-4.0% absolute hit rate loss for top-20 routes to start. token-saved down ~12% for those slices.
Tia: is this correlated with batching changes or kernel selection tweaks? any recent deploys?
Anya K: primary deploy was keyselector + batching heuristic tweak: reduced max_latency_ms from 16 -> 12 and switched key selector to prefix_hash_v2 to reduce collisions in long sequences.
Samir: i can pull flamegraphs but my hypothesis: prefix_hash_v2 is more sensitive to minor whitespace differences, so keys are more fragmented. that + tighter batching reduces opportunities for KV reuse.
Lee: confirmed in sampling — we see the same input text hashing to different keys when user metadata token appended, previously normalized away.
Tia: do we have a quick mitigation? revert key selector or add a normalizer in front?
Anya K: for immediate mitigation suggest two options:
- roll back to prefix_hash_v1 (fast rollback)
- add lightweight normalizer (strip trailing metadata tokens) and keep batching change
Samir: rollback seems lower risk. but we should instrument before/after to confirm.
perf-bot: sched-run: gather 30m windows, group by (model, route, tenant) and compute delta; alert if token_saved drop >10% and hit_rate drop >0.03
Lee: also adding dashboard panels: 1) per-route hit_rate trend (7d) 2) per-tenant token-saved waterfall 3) kernel/batch config vs hit_rate heatmap
Tia: dashboard query sketch: 
```
SELECT
  time_bucket('5m', ts) AS t,
  model, route, tenant,
  avg(prefix_cache.hit_rate) AS hit_rate,
  sum(tokens_saved) AS tokens_saved
FROM cache_metrics
WHERE ts > now() - interval '7 days'
GROUP BY t, model, route, tenant
ORDER BY t
```
Samir: nice. also add a small panel for key-entropy by route to identify churned keys.
Anya K: action items:
1) Samir -> run rollback to prefix_hash_v1 in staging and collect 1h comparison (owner: Samir)
2) Lee -> add dashboard panels + heatmap; add prefixed alert rules (owner: Lee)
3) Tia -> draft runbook entry for keyselector rollbacks and normalizer rationale (owner: Tia)
4) Anya -> coordinate canary if we reintroduce keyselector change with normalizer

Samir: starting rollback test now. will post perf-bot comparison link when ready.
perf-bot: job-complete: staging-compare link=https://perf.internal/reports/3054321987/compare overall_hit_rate_delta=+0.026 tokens_saved_delta=+8.4%
Lee: promising — staging rollback recovers most of the loss.
Tia: let's keep batching short-term (max_latency_ms=12) and revert keyselector, then iterate on normalizer + a/b canary for keyselector+normalizer pair.
Anya K: agreed. i'll schedule the rollback to prod canary window 03:45 UTC and ping infra. :thumbsup:
Samir: will grab sampling of affected tenants so CS can notify top impacted customers if needed.
Lee: follow-ups: add unit tests for key normalization and add a metric 'key_select.stability' showing % of identical keys across minor whitespace variants.
Tia: also we should document the tradeoff: lower batch latency can reduce prefix reuse; include that in the Optimize playbook.
Anya K: thanks all — keep updates in this thread. if perf-bot shows any new regressions tag me and @Lee.
Samir: ack
perf-bot: monitor: prefix_cache.hit_rate < 0.18 for 10m -> pager-signal (dev)
Anya K: closing loop later with retrospective notes and dashboard screenshots.
